title: Ride the cableway to Table Mountain's summit
description: The rotating cable car turns 360 degrees on the way up, but it shuts in high wind with no refund guarantee - check the live status online before you queue.

title: Hike Platteklip Gorge to the top of Table Mountain
description: The most direct route up, a relentless staircase of rock with almost no shade - start by 7am in summer and carry more water than feels necessary.

title: Tour Robben Island with a former political prisoner as guide
description: The ferry is the only way across and it cancels in swell with no warning - book the first sailing you can and build a buffer day into Cape Town for it.

title: Walk to the old lighthouse at Cape Point
description: Not actually the southernmost tip of Africa - that's Cape Agulhas, 150km east - but the funicular and cliff walk to the second lighthouse are worth the detour regardless.

title: Watch African penguins waddle at Boulders Beach
description: A colony that started with two breeding pairs in 1982 now numbers in the low thousands, even as the species crashes elsewhere on the coast - one of the few growing colonies left.

title: Walk the treetop canopy walkway at Kirstenbosch
description: The 'Boomslang' steel bridge curves through the canopy on the mountain's lower slopes. Come for the summer sunset concerts on the lawns if the dates line up - they sell out fast.

title: Photograph the coloured houses of Bo-Kaap
description: A real Cape Malay neighbourhood, not a museum piece - residents are increasingly unhappy with photographers blocking driveways, so keep to the street or book a paid walking tour that puts money back into the community.

title: Drive the cliffs of Chapman's Peak
description: A toll road cut into a sheer cliff face with over a hundred curves in 9km - it closes completely after heavy rain or rockfall, sometimes for days, so check conditions before making it your only route out.

title: Hop between estates on the Franschhoek Wine Tram
description: An open-sided tram-and-bus loop with several colour-coded lines - buy the ticket that includes tastings, not just transport, or you pay twice at each stop.

title: Taste at the historic wine estates of Stellenbosch
description: South Africa's oldest wine region, with Cape Dutch homesteads dating to the 1690s. Most estates charge a tasting fee that's waived if you buy a bottle, so ask before you sit down.

title: Watch southern right whales from the cliffs at Hermanus
description: One of the best land-based whale watching spots on earth - whales come within metres of the cliff path. The town even employs a 'whale crier' who blows a kelp horn to signal sightings.

title: Cruise the Knysna Lagoon to the Heads
description: Two sandstone cliffs guard one of the most treacherous harbour entrances in the world - ferries only run the gap in calm conditions, and captains have final say on the day.
A rocky peninsula loop past a seal colony and a cave used by humans 120,000 years ago - the full circuit needs a falling tide or the causeway section floods.
title: Hike the peninsula loop at Robberg Nature Reserve
Search out San rock art in the Cederberg
description: Sandstone formations, some of the darkest skies in the Western Cape, and rock art panels thousands of years old scattered across the range - a guide from the local community trust knows which overhangs to check.

title: Stand where the Indian and Atlantic oceans meet at Cape Agulhas
description: The actual southern tip of Africa, marked by a plain stone cairn rather than a monument - most tourists never make it here because Cape Point gets all the marketing.

title: Watch elephants at a waterhole in Addo Elephant National Park
description: Started with 11 elephants in 1931 to save the last survivors of a colonial hunting campaign; the park now holds one of the densest elephant populations on the continent and is malaria-free.

title: Cross the suspension bridge over the Storms River mouth
description: A bouncy swing bridge over a river mouth stained the colour of tea by fynbos tannins. Time it for low tide and you can scramble along the rocks beneath the bridge too.

title: Bungee jump the Bloukrans Bridge
description: 216 metres, long held as the highest commercial bridge bungee on earth. The walk out along the catwalk under the bridge deck before you jump is arguably scarier than the fall.

title: Hike the Wild Coast to Hole in the Wall
description: A sea arch punched clean through a rock island, reached along a coastline with almost no fences, resorts or crowds. The multi-day slackpacking trails between villages are the real draw, not the single viewpoint.

title: Drive the wilderness gorge road through Baviaanskloof
description: A UNESCO-listed wilderness area crossed by one unpaved mountain pass road with no fuel or phone signal for hours - a 4x4 or high-clearance vehicle is not optional after rain.

title: Visit Nelson Mandela's childhood village of Qunu
description: Mandela chose to be buried here rather than in a city, on a hillside above the school he attended as a boy. The Nelson Mandela Museum in nearby Mthatha is a better starting point than the village itself, which has few formal facilities.

Mist-wrapped indigenous forest said to have partly inspired Tolkien, who spent his early childhood in the district. Trail markers are inconsistent - pick up a map at one of the village lodges before setting out.
title: Walk the waterfall trails of Hogsback forest
Watch sunset over the Valley of Desolation
description: Dolerite pillars up to 120m tall stand above the Karoo plain in Camdeboo National Park, a short drive from one of South Africa's best-preserved Victorian towns.

title: Hike the chain ladders to the top of the Amphitheatre in the Drakensberg
description: Two permanently bolted chain ladders get you onto the escarpment where Tugela Falls drops nearly a kilometre - the world's second-highest waterfall, and at its most slippery right after the rain that makes it most spectacular.

title: Track rhino on foot in Hluhluwe-iMfolozi
description: Africa's oldest proclaimed game reserve, and the place that pulled the white rhino back from fewer than 100 animals to the population every southern African park now draws from.

title: Cruise the estuary for hippos and crocodiles at St Lucia
description: South Africa's first UNESCO World Heritage Site, where five ecosystems meet - the estuary holds one of the country's largest concentrated hippo populations, best seen on the afternoon cruise when they haul out to graze.

Sometimes called the biggest shoal on earth: billions of sardines moving up the coast pursued by dolphins, sharks and diving gannets. Timing and location shift every year and operators only confirm trips a few days out.
title: Dive the Sardine Run off the KwaZulu-Natal coast
Surf the Golden Mile in Durban
description: Warm Indian Ocean water year-round makes this one of the few places you can learn to surf comfortably in winter. Board hire and lessons line the promenade - haggle, prices aren't fixed.

title: Walk the battlefield at Isandlwana with a Zulu descendant guide
description: The site of the worst defeat the British Army suffered at the hands of an African army, in January 1879. White cairns mark where soldiers fell across the open veld, still visible from the original vantage points.

title: Dive the coral reefs of Sodwana Bay
description: The southernmost coral reefs in Africa, launched through the surf by tractor-towed boats rather than a harbour - a genuinely rough-and-ready start to some of the country's best diving.

title: Spot the Big Five on a dawn game drive in Kruger
description: Nearly two million hectares, and self-drive is not just possible but often better value than a guided tour - camps must be booked months ahead for the dry season when animals cluster at waterholes.

title: See the Three Rondavels from the rim of Blyde River Canyon
description: One of the largest 'green' canyons on earth, thickly forested rather than bare rock. Arrive by mid-morning - cloud regularly rolls in over the escarpment by early afternoon and can erase the view for hours.

title: Drive the Panorama Route past God's Window and Bourke's Luck Potholes
description: Bourke's Luck Potholes are sculpted cylinders carved by river sand at the confluence of two rivers - worth the short walk even though most cars stop only for God's Window ten minutes up the road.

title: Track leopards after dark in Sabi Sands
description: An unfenced private reserve on Kruger's western border where guides can drive off-road and spotlight at night - both banned inside Kruger itself, which is why leopard sightings here are so much more reliable.

An entire 1870s gold-rush town preserved as a national monument, corrugated iron roofs and all. The old cemetery includes the unmarked 'Robber's Grave', the only grave on the hill facing away from the rest.
title: Pan for gold in the museum town of Pilgrim's Rest
Drive the hairpins of Long Tom Pass
description: Named for the Boer siege gun abandoned near the summit in 1900, this pass over the Drakensberg escarpment is one of the steepest tarred roads in the country - fog rolls in fast, so keep headlights on even at midday.

title: See the golden rhino of Mapungubwe
description: The capital of a gold-trading kingdom that thrived here 800 years ago, centuries before Great Zimbabwe. The original golden rhino figurine lives in a university vault - the on-site museum shows a replica, which disappoints visitors who don't know that going in.

title: Watch Cape vultures wheel over Marakele National Park
description: Home to one of the largest Cape vulture breeding colonies on earth, on cliffs in the Waterberg massif. Also one of the few places to see a genuinely healthy black rhino population without Kruger's crowds.

title: Visit the sacred Lake Fundudzi with a Venda guide
description: South Africa's only true inland lake, formed by a landslide damming the Mutale River, and sacred to the Venda people as the home of ancestral spirits. Access is only permitted with a local guide, and some areas are off-limits entirely.

title: Walk among ancient cycads at the Modjadji Nature Reserve
description: The largest wild concentration of any single cycad species on the planet, on a forested hill traditionally ruled by the Rain Queen. The lineage of these plants predates the dinosaurs' extinction, though individual trees are merely centuries old.

title: Game drive the fever-tree forests of Pafuri
description: Kruger's remote northern tip, closer to Zimbabwe and Mozambique than to the main tourist camps, with baobabs and fever-tree forests found nowhere else in the park - and a fraction of the vehicle traffic.

title: Swim below Debengeni Falls near Tzaneen
description: A cold, clear pool beneath an 80m waterfall in the tea and forestry country outside Tzaneen - popular with locals on weekends, all but empty on weekdays.

title: Walk Vilakazi Street, the only street to house two Nobel laureates
description: Nelson Mandela's and Desmond Tutu's former homes stand a few hundred metres apart. Pair it with the Hector Pieterson Memorial a short walk away, which explains what the 1976 student uprising actually was before you see the bullet-marked plaques.

title: Enter the Apartheid Museum through the gate matching the race on your ticket
description: Your ticket is randomly stamped 'white' or 'non-white' and you enter through the corresponding turnstile, a small taste of a system that governed every part of daily life. Budget at least three hours - people who rush it regret it.

title: Descend into the Sterkfontein Caves at the Cradle of Humankind
description: More than a third of the world's early hominid fossils have come from this one set of limestone caves, including 'Little Foot', a near-complete skeleton over three million years old still partly embedded in rock when last checked.

Mandela, Gandhi and a string of later apartheid-era leaders were all held in the same prison complex that now shares a hill with South Africa's Constitutional Court - built deliberately on top of the old awaiting-trial block.
title: Tour the old Number Four prison at Constitution Hill
Browse street art and rooftop markets in Maboneng
description: A derelict industrial pocket of inner-city Johannesburg turned into a walkable arts district within about a decade - go on a Sunday for the market, and take a rideshare rather than walking after dark.

title: Spend a night at Lesedi Cultural Village
description: Five reconstructed homesteads representing different South African cultures, staffed by people from those communities rather than actors reciting a script - the evening feast and drumming runs late, so book the overnight option if you can.

title: Hike among sandstone cliffs in Golden Gate Highlands National Park
description: Sandstone cliffs that turn deep gold at sunset, with San rock art hidden in several overhangs along the Rhebok trail - snow is possible on the higher ground in winter, unusual for South Africa outside the Drakensberg.

title: Learn Basotho building techniques at the Basotho Cultural Village
description: A living-history village inside Golden Gate park showing four eras of Basotho homestead design side by side, built and staffed by the local community rather than an outside heritage authority.

title: Browse the gallery town of Clarens under the Maluti mountains
description: A one-square-mile village with more art galleries per resident than almost anywhere else in the country, ringed by sandstone peaks that turn orange in late afternoon light.

title: Spot the Big Five in an extinct volcanic crater at Pilanesberg
description: Malaria-free and two hours from Johannesburg, built inside the eroded rings of a 1.2-billion-year-old volcanic complex - the closest big-game park to Gauteng, which makes weekend self-drives realistic.

title: Ride the Valley of Waves at Sun City
description: A casino resort built in an old volcanic crater next to Pilanesberg, complete with an artificial wave pool and a bridge that shakes every hour to simulate an 'earthquake' - kitsch, but genuinely built for families rather than just gamblers.

title: Drive through the wildflower bloom in Namaqualand
description: One of the world's few desert biodiversity hotspots, when a few weeks of spring rain turn brown scrubland into carpets of orange and purple daisies almost overnight. The bloom only opens on sunny, windless days - a cloudy morning means the flowers stay shut.

title: Watch black-maned lions at a waterhole in the Kgalagadi
description: A red-dune desert park shared seamlessly with Botswana - no fence at the border, and a single permit covers both sides. The black mane on Kalahari lions is thought to help regulate heat loss, not just intimidate rivals.

title: Watch the Orange River drop through Augrabies Falls
description: A granite gorge that has swallowed the Orange River's floodwaters for millennia - in serious flood years the falls have shifted more water than Niagara, though most of the year it's a fraction of that.

title: Camp among giant quiver trees in the Richtersveld
description: A UNESCO cultural landscape still grazed under a communal Nama pastoral system that predates the park - one of the only deserts on earth with no permanent surface water at all, so every drop is trucked in or drawn from boreholes.

title: Look into the Big Hole, the largest hand-dug excavation on earth
description: Dug entirely by pick, shovel and bucket during the 1870s diamond rush, deep enough that miners once queued on a web of overhead cableways rather than ladders. A glass viewing platform now cantilevers out over the pit.

title: Stargaze under some of the clearest skies on earth at Sutherland
description: Home to the Southern African Large Telescope, the largest single optical telescope in the southern hemisphere, in a town so remote and dry that winter nights can drop below -10C - pack for far colder than the daytime desert heat suggests.
